questions.q: 0.5 mol of glucose is dissolved in 250 g of water. What is the molality of the solution?
questions.explain: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent (kg) = 0.5 / 0.250 = 2 mol kg^{−1}.

questions.q: Which of the following units of concentration depends on temperature?
questions.explain: Molarity involves the volume of the solution, and volume changes with temperature. The others depend on mass.

questions.q: What happens to the solubility of a gas in water if its partial pressure is doubled at constant temperature?
questions.explain: By Henry's law p = K_{H} x; so x (solubility) is proportional to p.

questions.q: K_{H} of N_{2} is 76.48 kbar at 293 K and 88.84 kbar at 303 K. At which temperature is N_{2} more soluble?
questions.explain: The smaller K_{H} is, the greater the solubility at the same pressure. K_{H} is smaller at 293 K, so the solubility is greater.

questions.q: In an ideal solution of A and B, p°_{A} = 400 mm Hg, p°_{B} = 100 mm Hg and x_{A} = 0.5. What is the total vapour pressure?
Which is correct for a solution showing positive deviation?
questions.explain: In a positive deviation the A–B attraction is weaker than A–A and B–B; so heat is absorbed on mixing and the volume increases.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a colligative property?
questions.explain: Density depends on the nature of the solute. Colligative properties depend only on the number of particles.

questions.q: What is the ratio (NaCl : glucose) of the depressions of freezing point of 0.1 m glucose and 0.1 m NaCl solutions (assume NaCl to be completely dissociated)?
questions.explain: i for NaCl = 2, for glucose = 1. ΔT_{f} = i K_{f} m, so the ratio is 2 : 1.

questions.q: What is the osmotic pressure of a 0.2 mol L^{−1} glucose solution at 300 K? (R = 0.083 L bar K^{−1} mol^{−1})
When does reverse osmosis take place?
options: When the pressure applied to the solution is less than the osmotic pressure
When the applied pressure equals the osmotic pressure
When the applied pressure is greater than the osmotic pressure
When two solutions are mixed without a membrane
questions.explain: If P > Π, solvent goes from the solution to the pure solvent. This is what is used in desalination.

questions.q: What is the approximate value of the van't Hoff factor (i) when acetic acid forms dimers in benzene?
questions.explain: When two molecules join to form one particle the number of particles is halved, so i ≈ 0.5; the molar mass becomes nearly double the true value.

questions.q: What will be the van't Hoff factor (i) if K_{2}SO_{4} is completely dissociated?
questions.explain: K_{2}SO_{4} → 2K^{+} + SO_{4}^{2−}; one formula unit gives 3 ions, so i = 3.
